name: DJIBOUTI

lead: Djibouti is a tiny country at the mouth of the Red Sea. Africa almost touches Arabia here. Every ship sailing between Asia and Europe passes its coast.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Built on coral reefs in the gulf

facts.label: Money
facts.sub: Pegged to the US dollar since 1949

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Djibouti sits in the Afar Triangle, where three tectonic plates (slabs of Earth's crust) slowly pull apart. Lake Assal is a white salt lake, 155 m below sea level, Africa's lowest point.
The coast opens onto the coral-filled Gulf of Tadjoura.
animals: Whale sharks, gentle giant fish, gather in the Gulf of Tadjoura from November to February. Dozens come for plankton (tiny floating food). Some are only two metres long.
The rare Djibouti spurfowl, a bird, lives in one small forest in the Goda Mountains. Fewer than 500 remain. At Lake Abbé, flamingos wade among limestone chimneys.
culture: Food here mixes Somali, Afar, Yemeni and French flavours. The national dish, skoudehkaris, is lamb and rice with spices like cardamom and cloves. Sticky xalwo sweets appear at every wedding.
Every afternoon, friends chew khat, a leafy plant, and talk politics for hours. The two main peoples are the Somali Issa and the Afar.
history: France arrived in 1862 and by the 1890s ruled it as French Somaliland. A railway to Ethiopia opened in 1917. It made the port vital for Ethiopia, which has no coast.
On 27 June 1977, 99.8% of voters chose independence. The new nation took its capital's name. It stayed calm while its neighbours fought. Now it rents land to foreign armies.
wows: About 12% of all world sea trade passes Djibouti's coast every day.
Djibouti hosts military bases from the USA, France, China, Italy and Japan at once.
Lake Assal is ten times saltier than the sea, so you float like in the salty Dead Sea.
The Afar Triangle is tearing apart, so a new ocean will form in about 10 million years.
Ethiopia, with 130 million people, sends over 95% of its trade through Djibouti.
Gulf of Tadjoura whale sharks are the youngest, on average, of any known gathering.
Africa's first cross-border electric railway links Djibouti and Addis Ababa, Ethiopia's capital.

myths.myth: A desert is always hot and sandy
myths.fact: A desert gets very little rain. Antarctica, a desert of ice, is the world's biggest.

myths.myth: Planet of the Apes was filmed at Lake Abbé
myths.fact: The 1968 film was shot in the United States.
